statements.text: Orphanet lists the prevalence of IgG4-related disease as unknown.
IgG4-related disease is an immune-mediated condition characterised by inflammation and progressive fibrosis, with a tendency to form tumefactive lesions in multiple organ sites.
The disease is characterised by dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltration, storiform fibrosis, and obliterative phlebitis on histological examination.
B cells play a central role in IgG4-related disease, as demonstrated by robust clinical responsiveness to B cell depletion therapy.
CD4+ T cells, including CD4+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes and a specific T follicular helper cell subset that contributes to IgG4 isotype switching, have been identified as key players in the disease.
Multiple self-antigens have been identified that promote B cell expansion in IgG4-related disease.
IgG4-related disease can affect virtually any organ in the body, with the most common clinical manifestations being pancreatitis and sialadenitis.

Common features include autoimmune pancreatitis, inflammatory pseudotumors, salivary gland disease with gland enlargement, lymphadenopathy, skin manifestations, and symptoms consistent with allergies or asthma.

Manifestations characterised by prominent tissue fibrosis, including retroperitoneal fibrosis, fibrosing mediastinitis, Riedel thyroiditis, orbital pseudotumor, and hypertrophic pachymeningitis, can be less responsive to glucocorticoid therapy than other types.
Relapses, either local or in other regions, are frequent during tapering of steroid dose.
Recurrence rates for IgG4-related disease are reported between 24% and 63% in various studies.
Persistent local inflammatory activity may result in permanent organ damage.
A probable increased risk of malignancies, including solid tumors and lymphoma, requires attention in long-term care of affected patients.

Laryngeal IgG4-related disease presents with hoarseness, dyspnea, or stridor, with supraglottic and subglottic involvement predominating and multilevel airway disease occurring in about one third of cases.
Serum IgG4 levels are frequently normal despite biopsy-proven IgG4-related disease.
Diagnosis of IgG4-related disease rests on the combined presence of characteristic histopathological appearance and increased numbers of IgG4+ plasma cells.

A quantitative histopathology-based scoring system using eight parameters, including IgG4+/CD138+ ratio, storiform fibrosis, and obliterative venulitis, demonstrated 95.74% sensitivity and 100% specificity for IgG4-related disease diagnosis.
Histopathological confirmation of laryngeal IgG4-related disease often requires deep submucosal or repeat biopsy after nondiagnostic superficial sampling.

Endoscopy and imaging of laryngeal IgG4-related disease show two main patterns: fibrostenotic circumferential narrowing resembling idiopathic subglottic stenosis and mass-like or polypoid lesions mimicking neoplasia.
A quantitative disease activity tool called the IgG4-RD Responder Index has been developed and validated through international, multi-centre investigations.
Classification criteria for IgG4-related disease were validated through international, multi-centre investigations.
Glucocorticoids are the first-line choice of treatment for IgG4-related disease.
In refractory cases, rituximab treatment has been used with good success.
Commonly used steroid-sparing agents are only partially effective in IgG4-related disease.
Surgical or interventional treatment may be necessary if complications arise in IgG4-related disease.
A distinction into proliferative and fibrotic phenotypes of IgG4-related disease has been proposed based on clinical presentation, pathological features, and response to immunosuppressive therapy.
Clinical trials are evaluating B-cell-targeted therapies including CAR T-cell approaches for relapsed or refractory IgG4-related disease.
Clinical trials are investigating lenalidomide as maintenance therapy to reduce relapse risk in patients with stable IgG4-related disease.
Clinical trials are evaluating inebilizumab for prevention of flare in IgG4-related disease.
Clinical trials are comparing treatment strategies combining prednisone with iguratimod or leflunomide in IgG4-related disease patients with superficial organ involvement.
Research is investigating the role of post-translational modifications on IgG4 antibodies in IgG4-related disease pathology.
Studies are examining the C5a-C5aR1 axis as a potential therapeutic target in IgG4-related disease.
Research is investigating trained immunity involvement in the pathogenesis of IgG4-related disease.
Clinical trials are evaluating gamma delta T cell therapy as a treatment for IgG4-related disease.
Imaging studies are comparing [18F]-AlF-FAPI-74 PET/CT with [18F]-FDG PET/CT for assessment of inflammation in IgG4-related disease.
A multicenter registry study in Japan is establishing clinical diagnostic criteria and treatment guidelines for IgG4-related disease using patient registry data.
